sourceState.repositoryStatus: Foundation scaffolding and package skeletons exist; feature implementation is not validated.
sourceState.engineImplementationNote: packages/engine/src/model/*, deck.ts, random.ts, scoring.ts, and index.ts are partial unvalidated implementation, not a completed phase.
sourceState.dependencyInstallation: Not installed or run as part of this handoff.

todos.title: Establishing repository foundation
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 0: initialize the repository and create the pnpm/Turborepo workspace, strict TypeScript, quality tooling, package skeletons, and baseline documentation.
exitCriteria: Workspace structure and package boundaries match the architecture documentation.
Strict TypeScript and quality-tooling configuration is present.
Baseline documentation describes the intended implementation contract.
resumeNotes: Treat this as complete foundation work, not evidence that feature behavior is implemented.
Do not install dependencies or infer runtime behavior from scaffolding alone.

todos.title: Documenting architecture and rules
todos.description: Create README, AGENTS guidance, architecture, canonical rules, and executable transition-contract documentation for the greenfield workspace.
exitCriteria: Architecture, rules, protocol, transition, and runbook documents are present.
Package boundaries, authority, privacy, timer, and persistence rules are explicit.
The transition contract enumerates commands, timers, rejection codes, and visibility.
resumeNotes: These documents are the authority for implementation decisions.
Update the relevant contract in the same change as any command, timer, or wire behavior change.

todos.title: Scaffolding workspace tooling
todos.description: Create root workspace configuration, package manifests, TypeScript configs, lint/format/test/build configuration, and package entry points without installing dependencies.

ownership.scope: Workspace configuration and package entry points

exitCriteria: Workspace manifests and project references are coherent.
Build, lint, format, typecheck, test, integration, and e2e entry points are declared.
No dependency installation is claimed until it is run on the implementation device.
resumeNotes: Use the pinned Node and pnpm versions from docs/runbook.md on the personal device.
Run baseline checks only after installing dependencies there.

todos.title: Defining executable rule contract
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 1: define canonical domain types, deterministic clock/RNG, card/deck/setup foundations, invariants, and the command/timer transition contract.

ownership.scope: Framework-free deterministic engine and contract alignment

exitCriteria: Canonical state, identifiers, cards, deck/setup, clock/RNG, and invariant APIs are implemented.
Reducer transitions cover the Phase 1 contract without I/O or wall-clock reads.
Engine tests prove deterministic setup, card conservation, and contract rejection behavior.
The partial files under packages/engine/src are reviewed and validated rather than assumed complete.
resumeNotes: packages/engine/src/model/*, deck.ts, random.ts, scoring.ts, and index.ts are partial unvalidated implementation, not a completed phase.
Preserve server authority, stable slots, seeded randomness, and the exact rules in docs/rules.md.

todos.title: Building core turn engine
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 2: build normal turns, Cambio final-turn queues, dealer rotation, reshuffling, end reasons, scoring, and cumulative standings.

ownership.scope: Engine normal turns, Cambio flow, round ends, and scoring

exitCriteria: Normal draw, replace, discard, turn advancement, Cambio queues, and dealer rotation are deterministic.
Stock reshuffle and every round-end reason follow the documented safe behavior.
Scoring and cumulative standings cover ties and caller adjustments.
Focused unit, property, and invariant tests pass.
resumeNotes: Do not implement powers, snaps, or server transport in this workstream.
Keep all state transitions pure and preserve the transition-contract rejection semantics.

todos.title: Building power and snap engine
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 3: build optional powers, snap races and penalties, opponent transfers, concurrent completion gates, timer generations, and deterministic removal.

ownership.scope: Engine powers, snaps, transfers, gates, timers, and removal effects

exitCriteria: All optional power stages, invalidation/reselection, and private reveal lifecycles are modeled.
Snap receive ordering, stale windows, wrong-snap penalties, successful snaps, and transfers are atomic.
Concurrent power/snap obligations and timer generations gate the next turn correctly.
Race, conservation, removal, and stock-exhaustion tests pass.
resumeNotes: A successful snap never triggers a power or opens another window.
Do not expose hidden card identities through engine events or client-facing structures.

todos.title: Defining protocol and privacy projections
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 4: create versioned Zod wire contracts, server mapping, per-viewer projections, public logs, fixtures, and automated privacy assertions.

ownership.scope: Versioned external DTOs and viewer-safe projection boundary

exitCriteria: Every command, message, view, and stable rejection code has a versioned schema.
One projection boundary produces viewer-safe snapshots, events, and logs.
Private reveals, hidden cards, credentials, and transient ranks are excluded from unauthorized views.
Schema fixtures and privacy assertions pass for every seat perspective.
resumeNotes: Protocol contains DTOs and validation, not game rule logic.
Never send raw domain events, reconnect secrets, buried discard ranks, or another player's private cards.

todos.title: Building real-time room server
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 5: build Fastify/WebSocket room actors, lobby lifecycle, guest sessions, host migration, command authorization, idempotency, timers, and broadcasts.

ownership.scope: Server-authoritative room actors and WebSocket lifecycle

exitCriteria: Room creation, join, resume, lobby configuration, start, commands, disconnects, and host migration are serialized per room.
Session generations, command idempotency, authorization, timer generations, and pause behavior are enforced.
Persistence is invoked before in-memory publication and broadcasts use viewer-safe projections.
Server integration tests cover multi-client lifecycle and stale-command behavior.
resumeNotes: The actor queue is the serialization boundary; socket callbacks must not mutate state directly.
Persistence details remain in the persistence workstream, but server interfaces must support them.

todos.title: Adding persistence and recovery
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 6: add SQLite migrations and repositories, transactional persist-before-publish, crash recovery, timer recovery policy, and 24-hour cleanup.

ownership.scope: SQLite schema, repositories, transactions, recovery, and retention

exitCriteria: Rooms, seats/sessions, snapshots, domain events, command receipts, and timers have migrations and repositories.
State, events, receipts, and timer rows commit atomically before broadcasts.
Restart recovery pauses rooms, refreshes generations/grace, and applies documented snap-window policy.
Idempotency survives restart and empty-room retention cleanup is race-safe and tested.
resumeNotes: Use SQLite WAL mode and the documented transactional ordering.
Do not persist private projection data or reconnect secrets in clear text.

todos.title: Building web session and lobby
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 7: build React routing, connection/state management, create/join/resume flows, host configuration, room sharing, and accessible lobby UI.

ownership.scope: React routing, connection state, session recovery, and lobby UX

exitCriteria: Create, join, resume, reconnect, and lobby configuration flows consume only protocol views.
Host and player states, errors, stale revisions, and connection transitions are accessible.
Room sharing never includes reconnect credentials.
Browser tests cover lobby and session journeys at responsive sizes.
resumeNotes: The web client never predicts authoritative rules or evaluates hidden state.
Keep online play separate from the dynamically loaded tutorial route.

todos.title: Building accessible game table
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 8: build responsive table rendering and every authoritative turn, power, snap, transfer, pause, removal, ready-up, and result interaction.
exitCriteria: Every legal server-described action has an accessible interaction and clear rejection handling.
Responsive stable-slot semantics, hidden-card placeholders, timers, pauses, history, scores, and results render correctly.
Power reveals and transient snap presentation events are shown only to entitled viewers.
Browser and accessibility tests cover complete turn, snap, transfer, pause, removal, and result flows.
resumeNotes: Never infer legality or card rank from layout, identifiers, or client state.
Use protocol view data and server legal-action hints only for UX.

todos.title: Adding presentation effects and history
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 9: add non-blocking card animations, sound controls, rank-safe action history, reduced-motion behavior, and effect backlog handling.

ownership.scope: Non-authoritative effects, sound, history presentation, and motion preferences

exitCriteria: Effects never delay or mutate authoritative state transitions.
Action history remains rank-safe and transient reveals are not logged.
Sound controls, reduced-motion behavior, and backlog handling are accessible and bounded.
Browser and accessibility checks cover effects during rapid event sequences.
resumeNotes: Presentation is downstream of the table and cannot introduce online game rules.
Prefer deterministic cleanup when messages arrive faster than animations complete.

todos.title: Building rules and tutorial
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 10: add the exact rules reference and dynamically loaded offline guided tutorial covering every required mechanic.

ownership.scope: Rules reference and offline guided tutorial

exitCriteria: Tutorial is dynamically loaded at /tutorial and remains offline without connecting to a room.
Guided scenarios cover setup, turns, powers, snaps, penalties, transfers, Cambio, scoring, and lifecycle concepts.
Rules reference matches docs/rules.md and uses the same authoritative engine behavior.
Tutorial and accessibility tests pass without bundling online server behavior into the main path.
resumeNotes: The tutorial is the only client-bundled use of engine and must use an isolated adapter.
Do not invent alternate rules or presets.

todos.title: Hardening the local release
todos.description: Implement plan Phase 11: add multi-client E2E, race/recovery/privacy/accessibility/soak coverage, production-like local serving, and final operating documentation.

ownership.scope: Release validation, hardening, local operations, and final documentation

exitCriteria: Multi-client journeys, races, recovery, privacy, accessibility, and soak scenarios pass.
Production-like local build and start paths are verified from a clean installed workspace.
No hidden-card, timer, persistence, or authority regressions remain.
Operating documentation records verified commands and known limitations.
resumeNotes: Run the full validation matrix only after all three dependencies are done.
A passing build does not replace rule, privacy, race, recovery, and accessibility coverage.
